dataList.content:
<I hereby confirm today’s close of business for the Sinners.>
<我批准罪人结束工作。>

Whether we're riding the bus through a forest or navigating the busboat over a vast lake, our daily routine changes very little.
不论是在森林里乘巴士，还是漂浮在宽广的大湖中央，我们每日的安排都没什么变化。

Thank you kindly. Starting now, you all will be given a maximum of 12 hours to partake in sleep and rest; the duration is subject to change. Have a good night.
谢谢。从现在开始，你们最多有12个小时可供睡眠和休息，时间可能会有所变动。祝各位有个美好的夜晚。

dataList.place: 梅菲斯托费勒斯 甲板
dataList.content:
The usual hubbub, followed by the usual leisurely idleness.
一如既往的吵嚷，随之而来的是一如既往的悠闲气氛。

I guess I'm not the only one starting to enjoy these normal, routine days.
我大概并不是唯一一个慢慢开始享受这种日常的人。

It wasn't by our choice, though. By now, I thought we'd be sailing vigorously across the waters toward the Lobotomy Corp. Branch located somewhere within U Corp.
但我们当然也不是自愿的。我想，我们应该正火速向着在U公司某处的脑叶公司支部航行……

But here we are, unable to leave the coastal side of the Great Lake, dawdling and twiddling our thumbs.
但现在我们的船甚至都没法离岸，只能在沿岸漂浮着来打发无聊的时间。

Well, it's not like there's been an accident. While Faust didn't elaborate, she explained that we had to wait for now.
嘛，倒也不是说有什么事故……浮士德解释说，我们现在还需要再等等。

If I were to hazard a guess, we were waiting here to complete some kind of an entry procedure like we did at K Corp. Either that, or we're waiting for someone(probably the Before team) to get in touch with us.
要我猜，一定像是K公司那样，需要我们完成某种入境程序，或者我们在等着谁（也许是清理部门先遣部队）的联络。

Which brings us here, surrounded by nothing but endless, endless water. The Sinners chattered about inane subjects before complaining about this immense boredom...
所以呢，我们就被困在大湖里，整天盯着无边无际的湖水……虽然罪人们在毫无意义地闲聊，随即又抱怨起这无聊透顶的时光……

But deep down, we were all exhausted from the unending onslaught of physically and emotionally draining happenings. Deep down, we all knew these leisurely days would not last.
但内心深处，我们都苦于这看不到头的、身体上和精神上的无尽折磨，也都深知这样平和的日子可不会长久下去。

So we each elected to enjoy this brief maritime respite in our own ways.
所以，我们都尽可能地享受着这短暂的海上假期。

Huff, Hurk...
哈、哈啊……

If thou needest mine assistance...
汝，真的还好吗？

... As I have repeatedly made myself clear...
……我已几次申明，但还是再回答一次……

I am... quite... alright...
我……还算安好……

Thy countenance, returning the contents within thy stomach to the Lake with such vigor... sayeth otherwise...
汝总是把汝吃下去的东西吐给大湖，这怎么算还好呢……

Except for Yi Sang, who had a surprisingly low tolerance for seasickness...
……除了李箱，他意外地容易晕船。

... This voyage was proving to be rather uneventful.
这次航行到现在还算平和。

<Yi Sang, the day's over. You can go back to your room now...>
<李箱，今天可以休息了。你可以回到房间去了……>

Oh... Shall I finally be freed from this suffering...?
哦……我终于能从这苦痛中解脱了吗……

<Seriously, I told you that you could rest in your room if you wanted.>
<说真的，你想的话可以一直在房间里休息。>

Our fellows must also have their share of suffering... I can not, in good faith, seek comfort only for myself.
有难同当之时……我怎么可能，仅寻求自己的安逸？

<You're the one with the biggest share of suffering right now...>
<现在已经没有人比你更痛苦了……>

While I wished that he'd be more reasonable with himself, I could see where he was coming from...
我是希望他能再多考虑考虑自己，但我也理解他这么做的缘由……

I thought better of it than to try to convince him otherwise. I instead chose to help Yi Sang to his room.
我没有再多说什么，而是把李箱扶进了他的房间。

I thank you, Dante. Then... until later.
感激不尽，但丁。然后……之后再见。

I waved at him and watched until he stumbled into his room and closed the door behind him.
当他跌跌撞撞地走进房间时，我向他挥手，并看着门关上。

Then I shall seek myself respite as well, Manager Esquire!
经理老爷！那吾也要先休息了！

<Yeah, rest well.>
<嗯，辛苦了。>

Don Quixote walked into the same Door that Yi Sang had walked into. I could get a blurry glimpse into her room over her shoulder.
堂吉诃德走进了李箱刚走进的同一扇门，我能从她肩头微微瞥见房间里的样子。

I couldn't get a good look at it... but it was certainly not the same room Yi Sang had walked into.
虽然看得并不清楚，但那和李箱走进的房间完全不同。

<I see these doors every day... but I still don't get it.>
<我每次见到这些门都不明白……>

I should probably be used to this by now, but it's still pretty fascinating how the rooms changed based on who opened the doors.
我早就应该习惯了。但是房间根据开门的人不同，在一开一合之间变幻的样子，还是让我觉得很不可思议。

I turned, leaving their shut door behind, ready to return to my room.
我转过身来，关上了他们的门，准备走进我的房间。

There's a door immediately to the right side of that demarcation of the corridor we're not allowed to cross.
走廊上那条禁止通行分界线的右边，还有一扇门。

Within that door is a space somewhat different from the Sinners' rooms.
那扇门里的，是不同于罪人们的房间的空间。

In there were the wooden door to my room and the metal door leading into the Mirror Dungeons.
那里有通往我的房间的木门，和通往镜像迷宫的铁门。

The doors leading to the Luxcavation Dungeons and the recently-opened door to the Refraction Railway also come into view.
还有通往采光迷宫的，然后最近刚打开而通往折射轨道的门也看得见。

<No new doors... yet.>
<现在……还没有新的门。>

For no reason in particular, I creak those doors open and take a quick peek inside to see if anything changed.
我悄悄打开了一个门缝，看看里面是否有什么变化。

Well... I've never actually managed to catch any changes myself, but... who knows?
好吧，我自己确实没看出来有什么变化，但……万一呢。

Maybe I'll notice something worth keeping to myself...
也许会发生一些只有我自己知道的事情。

... Which I should probably report to Faust.
……那样的话，我就应该向浮士德报告了吧？

Something must've caught wind of my rather mischievous thought.
不知道是不是因为我这不太合适的念头，

An ear-splitting siren blares all the way here from the other end of the bus.
一声震耳欲聋的警报响彻了巴士内部。

Blimey, what the hell is...
可恶，又怎么了……

dataList.place: 梅菲斯托费勒斯 船舱
dataList.content:
Oh boy, this again?
啊，又来？

M.E. Kill the volume...
耳·裂。把音量搞低点……

I spun around to face the other side of the corridor. The Sinners, alarmed by the noise, were one by one peeking out of their rooms.
我慌忙转身看向走廊的另一边，听到警报的罪人们一个接一个地从房间里探出头来。

They were used to this siren by now, but that didn't change the unpleasant fact that their sweet private hours were disturbed...
因为响过很多次，罪人们都很熟悉这种警报了，但他们甜蜜的私人时光因此被打断时还是很不爽……

Well met, Dante. Let us observe this disturbance together.
但丁，贵安。让我们来看看情况吧。

<O-okay.>
<噢，好。>

... I accompanied Faust to the helm.
……我和浮士德一起来到了驾驶席所在的位置。

She fiddled with a few buttons, and shut off the alarm. Incomprehensible, complicated-looking letters began to fill the round screen.
浮士德调整了一些按钮，然后关掉了警报。圆形的屏幕上开始浮现出难以理解的复杂字符。

<... Is that a new room?>
<……新的房间要来了吗？>

Even Faust needs a moment to decipher.
就算是浮士德，解码也是需要一些时间的。

<Right, right...>
<好、好的……>

The siren always comes without warning.
这些震耳欲聋的警报声总是毫无征兆地响起来。

And with it appeared the Mirror Dungeons, the Luxcavation Dungeons, and the Refraction Railways.
而且，镜像迷宫、采光迷宫和折射轨道都随着这样的警报而出现。

<I don't know if it's relevant, but... I didn't see anything that would indicate activity when I checked the Railway door earlier.>
<我不确定是不是有关，但是……我之前查看轨道线路的门的时候，没发现有什么情况。>

It is unlikely that anything new would appear from that entrance.
那个入口大概不会有什么变化了。

I find it difficult to believe that the next Line would arrive so soon when the glow of the door leading to Line 2 has yet to go out.
二号线门口的荧光熄灭之前，下一条轨道线路应该是不会来临的。

<I guess you're right.>
<你说得对。>

The first Railway really took me by surprise when it appeared.
第一条轨道线路出现的时候，可吓了我一跳。

A new door had appeared before us, its edges shimmering with a blue glow. And when we entered it...
新的门出现在我们眼前，其门框上闪着蓝色的荧光。当我们进入那门的时候……

A mysterious vehicle was just sitting there, waiting for us.
一辆神秘的载具就在那里，静静等待着我们。

Its appearance somewhat resembled that of Mephistopheles... but it was also patently clear that I'd never seen anything like it before. An odd feeling.
其形态多少和梅菲斯托费勒斯有所相似……但我很确信我从未见过那样的东西，真是奇怪的感觉。

I see that your first encounter with the train has left a strong impression, Dante.
能看得出来第一条轨道给你留下了深刻的印象，但丁。

Well, I recall that you had a rather violent reaction when I entered the train to observe its interiors.
我是说，当浮士德进入列车观察内部状况时，你的反应很激烈。

<Come on, I wasn't the only one that freaked out. Everyone did...>
<当时被惊到的又不止我一个，大家都……>

What if that thing left the Station before the rest of us got on?
幸好，那个交通工具好像必须同时载着我和罪人们才会出发。

... Was what I wanted to say if Faust hadn't already turned around from the screen, to which her eyes had been metaphorically glued for a while, and walked away.
要不是浮士德突然转过身去，离开了那已经死盯了好一会儿的屏幕，我就要说出这句话来了。

<This wasn't it, then?>
<……不是那样吧？>

No. This particular volatility is not something we can utilize.
嗯。我们大概无法利用此次波动。

<Right... I thought it was an awkward time for a new door to appear. Too soon, too soon.>
<我也是觉得这么早就开新的门……有点快得出奇了。>

The Dungeons and the Railways appeared at 'awkward times' as well, Dante. I recommend that you refrain from settling into a premature conclusion. A new variable may present itself at any moment.
迷宫和轨道第一次出现的时间也很“奇怪”，但丁。因为新的变量任何时候都可能出现，所以建议您不要抱有过时的固定观念。

... Moreover...
……还有，

If this volatility has triggered an alarm in Mephistopheles' engine, then it naturally follows that a new door has appeared at an indeterminate location down the corridor.
如果这种波动触发了梅菲斯托费勒斯引擎的警报，之后新的门通常就会在走廊里的某处出现。

This may reveal a space from which one could never return. It is best that we keep track of these incidents.
这也许会打开一个根本没有回头路的空间。所以我们最好要对这些空间有确切的把握。

<Even Heathcliff won't do anything like that again. ... Probably.>
<就算是希斯克利夫也不会再做一次那样的事了吧……大概。>

... As per my last advice to you, a premature conclusion is...
……不要抱有过时的固定观念。

Regardless, no serious issues have been detected at this moment. ... It would be most apt that we enjoy our remaining rest period.
不论如何，这次并没有发现任何严重的问题……我们回去享受剩下的休息时间会比较妥当。

Now, if you will excuse me. Rest well, Dante.
那么，我先失陪了。好好休息，但丁。

With those as her parting words, Faust disappeared into her room in her usual manner.
随着她告别的话语，浮士德像往常一样消失进了她的房间里。

Left alone again, on this bus... boat.
我又被孤独地丢在了这巴士……船里。

I looked at the numerous letters displayed on the screen.
我盯着屏幕上还未消去的无数字符。

Numbers. Unintelligible letters. Drawings and symbols depicting something.
数字、难以辨识的字符、似乎象征着什么东西的图象和符号。

I had to shake my clock head after staring at that dizzying sight for a while.
盯久了那些飘来飘去的字符，我猛地摇了摇头。

<I wonder if this is how Yi Sang felt earlier... I'm starting to feel nauseous.>
<李箱之前晕船的感觉大概就是这样吧……我开始觉得有些晕了。>

I was barely able to hold back the vertigo from setting in. Time to saunter back to my room.
我忍着头晕起身，摇摇晃晃地向着房间里走去。

Let's turn in early tonight...
今天……还是早点休息吧。
